findings.title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of one-way hash
findings.body: Backup codes are encrypted with symmetricEncrypt/symmetricDecrypt using CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (see also setup.ts line 68), the same way the TOTP secret is stored. Unlike the TOTP secret, backup codes never need to be recovered in plaintext for comparison — they only need equality checking, so they should be hashed with a one-way function (e.g. bcrypt/argon2) like passwords. Storing them with reversible encryption means that if CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is ever compromised, every user's full set of backup/recovery codes can be recovered in plaintext, defeating the purpose of a second factor recovery mechanism.

findings.title: Backup code component incorrectly named 'TwoFactor'
findings.body: The default-exported function in BackupCode.tsx is declared as `function TwoFactor({ center = true })` instead of `function BackupCode(...)`. This is clearly copy-pasted from TwoFactor.tsx and not renamed. While the default export still works at the module level, React DevTools, error stack traces, and displayName-based debugging will show 'TwoFactor' for what is actually the backup-code input component, causing confusion when diagnosing issues in either component.

findings.title: backupCodes state is untyped, inferred as never[]
findings.body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` has no generic type argument, so TypeScript infers the state type as `never[]`. The code later calls `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and `backupCodes.map((code) => ...)` where `code` is typed as `never`, relying on `body` being implicitly `any` to avoid a compile error. This should be `useState<string[]>([])` to get proper type safety for the `code` parameter and avoid incorrect typing silently propagating through the component.

findings.title: No e2e coverage for the actual backup-code login/disable flows
findings.body: The PR adds the ability to log in with a backup code and to disable 2FA using a backup code (the core new functionality described in the PR), but the only test change exercises the backup-code download/copy UI during setup. The TODO comment itself acknowledges 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup', and the PR checklist states no tests were added proving the feature works. This leaves the primary new behavior (backup-code authentication, IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes error handling) completely untested.

findings.title: Backup codes are persisted to the DB before 2FA setup is confirmed
findings.body: setup.ts generates and stores encrypted backupCodes (and the TOTP secret) in the database immediately after password confirmation, while twoFactorEnabled remains false. If the user abandons the setup flow (e.g. closes the modal after seeing the QR code without entering a valid TOTP code), the newly generated backup codes remain stored against the user's account indefinitely even though 2FA was never actually enabled, until the user restarts setup (which overwrites them) or disables 2FA. This leaves sensitive recovery codes persisted for an account state that doesn't reflect them being issued/used.

findings.title: Backup codes Blob URL is leaked if the dialog is closed without restarting setup
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is called in handleSetup and only revoked via `if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)` the next time handleSetup runs. If the user completes the enable flow (closing the modal via the Close button) or cancels without re-opening setup, the created object URL is never revoked, leaking the Blob for the lifetime of the page/session.

findings.title: Misleading 'missing_backup_codes' message references a non-existent settings feature
findings.body: The string `missing_backup_codes`: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." implies there is a dedicated settings action to regenerate backup codes. No such feature was added in this PR — the only way to get a fresh set of backup codes is to fully disable and re-enable two-factor authentication. This message will confuse users looking for a 'regenerate backup codes' option in settings that doesn't exist.
